Basic Measures Of Dispersion Key Concept

According to Spiegel, the degree to which numerical data tend to spread about an average value is called the variation or dispersion of data.

Range Key Concept

It is defined as the difference between the maximum value of the variable and the minimum value of the variable in the distribution.

Quartile Deviation Key Concept

The Descriptive Statistics 76 semi-interquartile range which is also known as Quartile Deviation (QD) is given by Quartile Deviation (QD) = (Q3 – Q1) / 2 Relative measure of Q.D.

Mean Deviation Key Concept

Mean deviation is defined as average of the sum of the absolute values of deviation from any arbitrary value viz.

📌 Key Takeaways

Section-by-Section Study Breakdown

3.2 Basic Measures of Dispersion

  • According to Spiegel, the degree to which numerical data tend to spread about an average value is called the variation or dispersion of data.
  • Actually, there are two basic kinds of measures of dispersion: (i) Absolute measures and (ii) Relative measures.
  • The absolute measures of dispersion are used to measure the variability of a given data expressed in the same unit, while the relative measures are used to compare the variability of two or more sets of observations.
  • Following are the different measures of dispersion: 1.

3.2.1 Range

  • It is defined as the difference between the maximum value of the variable and the minimum value of the variable in the distribution.
  • The demerit is that it is a crude measure because it is using only the maximum and the minimum observations of variable.
  • However, it still finds applications in Order Statistics and Statistical Quality Control.
  • It can be defined as Min Max X X R − = where, Max X : Maximum value of variable and Min X : Minimum value of variable.

3.2.2 Quartile Deviation

  • The Descriptive Statistics 76 semi-interquartile range which is also known as Quartile Deviation (QD) is given by Quartile Deviation (QD) = (Q3 – Q1) / 2 Relative measure of Q.D.
  • Similarly, 3N/4 = 21 and 21st observation falls in the interval 30-40.
  • It is often suggested to calculate it from the median because it gives least value when measured from the median.
  • The deviation of an observation xi from the assumed mean A is defined as (xi – A).

3.2.3 Mean Deviation

  • Mean deviation is defined as average of the sum of the absolute values of deviation from any arbitrary value viz.
  • It is often suggested to calculate it from the median because it gives least value when measured from the median.
  • The deviation of an observation xi from the assumed mean A is defined as (xi – A).

  • Taking a square of the deviation is a better technique to get rid of negative deviations.
